title: Distinct Subsequences
pattern: 2-D DP: use the letter or skip it
statement: Given strings `s` and `t`, return the number of distinct **subsequences of `s`** that are equal to `t` — the number of ways to delete letters from `s` so that `t` remains.
idea: Let `dp[i][j]` be the number of ways to form the first `j` letters of `t` from the first `i` letters of `s`.

Look at the last letter of that prefix of `s`. It can always be **skipped**: `dp[i − 1][j]` ways. If it equals the last needed letter of `t`, it can also be **used** for it: then the earlier letters must form the rest, `dp[i − 1][j − 1]` ways.
An empty `t` can be formed in exactly one way from any prefix (delete everything), so the first column is 1.

complexity.timeWhy: One cell per pair of prefix lengths.
complexity.spaceWhy: The table (one row would be enough).

steps.text: Our example: **`s = "babag", t = "bag"`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
First column: the **empty** target can be formed from any prefix of `s` in exactly 1 way — use no letters at all.
